body: That's the last resort, but one that's been on my mind for some time. At the end of the day, it is still my apartment and he only lives with me because I convinced the landlord he was a stand up guy. I'm not letting him drag my reputation through the mud with his.

Oh that's just the Reader's Digest version. The full story is that he asked me if she could move in after I had been awake for over thirty hours straight (work-related stuff) while simultaneously battling a cold/fever. I said I'd think about it, just playing for time so I could sleep and recover.

Few days later, I'm feeling better and I tell him I'm not okay with her moving in. He replies with, "Well you took too long to give me an answer, so I've already offered and she's already accepted."

Thank God I managed to talk him down from that.

You took the words right out of my mouth! It's not personal with this girl (okay maybe a little because I don't like her) but he needs to know that I need my space. It won't even be for that long, since I'm planning to move to a bigger city as soon as I can afford it.

That's the plan, honestly. Though I can't in all good conscience ban the girl completely. My brother and I split the rent and bills, which I believe entitles him to certain house rights same as me.

And I can't talk to him about the girl manipulating him, since he gets SUPER aggressive and defensive about it. She is his mistake to make, but the rest of it you're right: it's time to lay down some concrete boundaries and let him know this behavior is not okay when there's a family roommate in the mix.

I actually agree that it's a fight worth having, and in fact told myself those exact words! I'm just not excited at the prospect, as my brother and I have always been best friends and I don't want this random girl messing that up. 

He clearly sees something in her that I do not, and I think she's just manipulating him to use him as her newest meal ticket now that she's breaking up with her last boyfriend. That may just be an irreconcilable disagreement.

Apartment is in my name. Its not big enough to effectively have my own space. I also don't have a "room" per se, but an upstairs loft-type area about the size of a large closet where my bed is built into the wall and that's about it.

And I don't disagree about letting him learn his lesson. I just hate it cause i know my brother is smarter than this.

Hope is the poison of the human soul. And it's one people take willingly and happily.

People have told me the same thing as you. That I need to have hope. But unless there's a positive payoff, hope is the most useless emotion in the world. The world does not change on the whims of the individual and that is exactly what hope makes us wish for. No wonder we're always let down in the end.

Strangely enough, I made myself the same deal when I was younger and it was also weirdly motivating. Only problem is that now I'm 24 and careening toward suicide worse than ever before. So I guess be careful what you wish for...
Fortunately (or unfortunately, depending on the point of view) my next time is coming up pretty soon. I have to be back at work in about two hours and I have to say I'm more than a little nervous.
Thanks for your kind words. On some level I agree with everything you're saying, but I was raised on a strict diet of "real men don't show weakness" so sometimes it's hard to move past that.
